description: Each rating's average length is compared with the mean length over all individual films.

b.request: Keep ratings whose AVG(length) exceeds the film-level AVG(length) over all non-NULL films, then keep those whose AVG(length) also exceeds the mean of the first-cut ratings' AVG(length) values, and return one row with AVG of the survivors' averages, AVG(their averages minus the film-level mean), and AVG(their averages minus the first-cut mean), unrounded
b.sql: WITH film_level AS (SELECT AVG(length) AS overall_avg FROM film WHERE length IS NOT NULL), rating_avgs AS (SELECT rating, AVG(length) AS avg_len FROM film WHERE length IS NOT NULL GROUP BY rating), first_cut AS (SELECT r.rating, r.avg_len FROM rating_avgs r CROSS JOIN film_level f WHERE r.avg_len > f.overall_avg), first_mean AS (SELECT AVG(avg_len) AS cut_mean FROM first_cut), survivors AS (SELECT fc.avg_len FROM first_cut fc CROSS JOIN first_mean m WHERE fc.avg_len > m.cut_mean) SELECT AVG(s.avg_len) AS avg_of_survivor_avgs, AVG(s.avg_len - f.overall_avg) AS avg_gap_to_film_mean, AVG(s.avg_len - m.cut_mean) AS avg_gap_to_first_cut_mean FROM survivors s CROSS JOIN film_level f CROSS JOIN first_mean m;

c.request: Which film ratings have an average `length` (ignoring missing lengths) that is longer than average? Of those ratings, keep only the ones that also run longer than the mean of their own average lengths. Give one row with: the mean of the remaining ratings' average lengths, how far on average they sit above that first average, and how far on average they sit above the mean of the ratings that passed the first cut. No rounding. Each rating's average length is compared with the mean length over all individual films.
c.sql: WITH overall AS (SELECT AVG(length) AS overall_avg FROM film WHERE length IS NOT NULL), by_rating AS (SELECT rating, AVG(length) AS avg_len FROM film WHERE length IS NOT NULL GROUP BY rating), first_cut AS (SELECT b.rating, b.avg_len FROM by_rating b CROSS JOIN overall o WHERE b.avg_len > o.overall_avg), first_mean AS (SELECT AVG(avg_len) AS fc_mean FROM first_cut), second_cut AS (SELECT f.rating, f.avg_len FROM first_cut f CROSS JOIN first_mean m WHERE f.avg_len > m.fc_mean) SELECT AVG(s.avg_len) AS mean_remaining_avg_length, AVG(s.avg_len - o.overall_avg) AS avg_gap_above_overall_avg, AVG(s.avg_len - m.fc_mean) AS avg_gap_above_first_cut_mean FROM second_cut s CROSS JOIN overall o CROSS JOIN first_mean m

a.request: Compute each film `rating`'s average `length`, ignoring missing lengths. As the baseline, take the average length over all films, with each film counting equally. Keep the ratings whose average length is above that baseline. Among those ratings, take the mean of their average lengths and keep only the ratings that are above that mean too. Return one row with: the mean of the remaining ratings' average lengths, the mean amount by which they exceed the baseline, and the mean amount by which they exceed the kept ratings' mean. Do not round anything.
a.sql: WITH rating_avg AS (SELECT rating, AVG(length) AS avg_len FROM film WHERE length IS NOT NULL GROUP BY rating), baseline AS (SELECT AVG(length) AS base_len FROM film WHERE length IS NOT NULL), above_baseline AS (SELECT r.rating, r.avg_len FROM rating_avg r CROSS JOIN baseline b WHERE r.avg_len > b.base_len), kept_mean AS (SELECT AVG(avg_len) AS mean_len FROM above_baseline), final_set AS (SELECT a.rating, a.avg_len FROM above_baseline a CROSS JOIN kept_mean k WHERE a.avg_len > k.mean_len) SELECT AVG(f.avg_len) AS mean_of_remaining_avgs, AVG(f.avg_len - b.base_len) AS mean_excess_over_baseline, AVG(f.avg_len - k.mean_len) AS mean_excess_over_kept_mean FROM final_set f CROSS JOIN baseline b CROSS JOIN kept_mean k;

d.request: Among the film ratings whose average `length` (ignoring missing lengths) is above the overall average, keep those whose average length is also above the mean of their own average lengths. For that remaining set, give one row with: the mean of their average lengths, how far on average they sit above that mean, and how far on average they sit above the mean of the ratings that passed the first cut. Do not round. Note that each rating's average length should be compared against the mean length across all individual films.
d.sql: WITH overall AS (SELECT AVG(length) AS overall_avg FROM film), r AS (SELECT rating, AVG(length) AS avg_len FROM film WHERE length IS NOT NULL GROUP BY rating), first_cut AS (SELECT r.rating, r.avg_len FROM r CROSS JOIN overall o WHERE r.avg_len > o.overall_avg), m1 AS (SELECT AVG(avg_len) AS mean1 FROM first_cut), second_cut AS (SELECT fc.rating, fc.avg_len FROM first_cut fc CROSS JOIN m1 WHERE fc.avg_len > m1.mean1), m2 AS (SELECT AVG(avg_len) AS mean2 FROM second_cut) SELECT m2.mean2 AS mean_of_avg_lengths, AVG(sc.avg_len - m2.mean2) AS avg_above_mean, AVG(sc.avg_len - m1.mean1) AS avg_above_first_cut_mean FROM second_cut sc CROSS JOIN m1 CROSS JOIN m2;
